validated_work_order.understanding:
All three review findings from PR #67 still reproduce against current main (6ee19f7).

(1) Comment attachment ambiguity at packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts:23-31. Line 25 reads 'installed along with the console spies', where 'installed' has as its subject 'the global.fetch spy this file's beforeAll installed'. A reader can attach the console clause to 'installed' and conclude the beforeAll installs console spies. It does not: beforeAll (lines 17-21) contains zero occurrences of the string 'console', and patchFetchForSqlJS (packages/loot-core/src/mocks/util.ts:67-82) touches only global.fetch. All five console spies are created inside individual test bodies (lines 81, 116-118, 160, 311, 379). The file's own describe-level comment at lines 46-51 already states the correct fact, contradicting the reading line 25 permits. Only occurrence of the phrasing in the repo; the sibling index.electron.test.ts makes no fetch-spy claim and has no equivalent ambiguity.

(2) Release note keep-or-drop, left open. upcoming-release-notes/clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md is on main and validates (category Maintenance in categoryOrder, author Shivam-Fl not in NON_PERSON_AUTHORS, one-line body). The review is right that the cited gate is inert: .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml exists but no workflow references it, and .sdlc/config.yml:157-172 runs only typecheck/lint/unit. I am KEEPING the note on grounds other than the gate.

(3) PR #67 title lacks the mandatory [AI] prefix. Reproduces as a fact (gh pr view 67 --json title returns 'fix: Follow-ups from #58: 2 from the review', merged 2026-10-04), but it is not a defect this issue can fix and the review's 'Fix' line points at the wrong thing. The title is not hand-authored: .sdlc/bin/open-pr.mjs:138 sets it as `'--title', `fix: ${issueData.title}`` with no [AI] anywhere in that file. PRs #53, #59, #60, #64, #65 are titled the same way because every PR goes through that line. .sdlc/bin/** is in forbidden_paths (.sdlc/config.yml:218) and .sdlc/** is framework, so the fix belongs to the pipeline's plumbing, not this repository's code. Out of scope, with the location named.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Finding 1 is a dangling-preposition attachment in prose: 'along with the console spies' can bind to 'installed' rather than to 'takes down', producing a claim about the beforeAll that the code contradicts. Nothing executes wrongly — the sentence is wrong, not the test. Finding 2 is not a defect but an open judgement the review declined to close. Finding 3 is a one-line omission in the pipeline's own PR-opening code, outside this repository's changeable surface.
validated_work_order.approach:
One comment-only edit. Nothing else changes, no file added or deleted, no behaviour moves.

The fix is the review's first option (move the console clause off 'installed' so the attachment is explicit), not the second (drop the clause), because lines 46-51 carry the count but not the beforeAll contrast, and the beforeAll contrast is the whole reason the comment exists.

One deliberate divergence from the review's suggested wording: it proposed '...along with the console spies each test installs'. That introduces a fresh factual error — only 5 of the 10 tests install a console spy, so 'each test installs' is false of the other five. This order uses 'any console spies a test has installed', true now and still true if a sixth test grows a spy. QA step 3 fails the PR if the reviewer's wording appears.

On finding 2: KEEP the note. The review is right the original justification does not hold, but the note does not need it, and the review's 'to drop it' option is the more disruptive. Three reasons, in the order they decided it: (a) the convention that actually asks for the note is documented and gate-independent — packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:105 lists 'Add a release note' as a PR step, and :120 says a body should be 'non-technical (unless the category is "Maintenance")', the one thing this note's body would breach being explicitly exempted; (b) the note is already merged, so deleting it is a new PR whose entire content is removing an entry from the changelog about to be published — more visible to readers than the note ever was, and the review's 'PR #55 did' comparison does not carry over because #55 never had a note to remove; (c) recursion — a PR whose only content is deleting a release note is itself a change the convention wants a note for.

Recorded as a decision rather than deferred, because the implementer must not be left to make it. Review may disagree cheaply: the note's category, author and body all validate today. What is NOT upheld is the original reasoning — the gate argument is wrong and must not be repeated in the commit message.

On finding 3: no file changes; see out_of_scope.

files.change: In the block comment immediately above the beforeEach at line 32 (currently lines 23-31), replace those lines with exactly the given text, rewrapped so every line is at most 79 characters, matching the width the surrounding comment block already uses. Two things change and nothing else: a comma is added after 'installed', and the noun phrase becomes 'any console spies a test has installed' in place of 'the console spies'. The em dash on the 'compiled wasm —' line is U+2014 and must be preserved. Every other clause, including the whole fetch-patch history from 'Nothing breaks today...' through '...can no longer outrun it', stays byte-identical. Do not touch the beforeAll at 17-21, the beforeEach at 32, the describe-level comment at 42-60, or any test body.
files.why: The only finding that is a defect in this repository's source. A prose fix, so no test can make it correct — the test can only confirm the file still runs, which is why the exact wording was chosen against the code by hand rather than left to the implementer.

acceptance.check: The comment above the beforeEach no longer permits reading the console-spy clause as attached to 'installed': it reads 'installed, along with any console spies a test has installed', with a comma after 'installed'.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Not browser-observable and not test-observable — it is a claim about prose. Read lines 23-31 and confirm the sentence. Then confirm `grep -rn 'installed along with the console spies' packages/` returns no hits (exactly one hit, line 25, before this change) and that `grep -c 'any console spies a test has installed' packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts` returns 1.

acceptance.check: The factual claim the reworded sentence makes is true of the code: the beforeAll installs no console spy, and the console spies restoreAllMocks tears down are the ones individual tests install.
acceptance.how_to_verify: The invariant that must hold: every spyOn(console, ...) call site lies inside an it(...) body, none inside the beforeAll at 17-21. `sed -n '17,21p' packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts | grep -c console` must return 0. `grep -n 'spyOn(console' packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts` must return only lines inside test bodies — five sites at 81, 116-118, 160, 311, 379, the fifth wrapped across three lines at 116-118 that a single-line grep for 'vi.spyOn(console' misses. If the implementer had used the review's 'each test installs', this check fails: only 5 of 10 tests install a spy.

acceptance.check: The edited file still runs: the loot-core web suite for this file passes, with the fetch-patch regression test among the passing cases.
acceptance.how_to_verify: CI runs `yarn test` from the repo root, reaching this file via packages/loot-core's test:web script (ENV=web vitest --run -c vitest.web.config.ts; the file is named in that config's include list at packages/loot-core/vitest.web.config.ts:9). Confirm all 10 tests pass, including 'keeps the sql.js wasm fetch patched for each test, not just the first'. This checkout has no node_modules, so the suite cannot be run locally — it is a CI check.

acceptance.check: The release note is kept unmodified: upcoming-release-notes/clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md still exists with byte-identical contents and still validates.
acceptance.how_to_verify: `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/` must return empty — this change adds, edits and deletes no release note. Category 'Maintenance' is in categoryOrder (packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs:17-22), author 'Shivam-Fl' is not in NON_PERSON_AUTHORS (line 30), body is one line, so packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs would pass it if it ran.

qa_script: Confirm the diff is one file: `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` shows packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts only, and no file under upcoming-release-notes/ appears.
Read lines 23-31 and check AC-1 by eye: the comma after 'installed' is present and the console clause reads 'any console spies a test has installed'.

Run AC-2's grep commands and confirm the beforeAll contains no console spy and all five console spy sites are inside test bodies. Treat the review's wording 'the console spies each test installs' as a FAILURE if it appears — only 5 of 10 tests install a spy.
Confirm the em dash on the 'compiled wasm —' line survived as U+2014 and was not replaced with a hyphen.
Confirm `yarn typecheck` and `yarn lint` are clean and CI's `yarn test` passes all 10 tests in the file (no node_modules in this checkout, so the suite runs in CI).

Confirm upcoming-release-notes/clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md is untouched and still present — its deletion is the one release-note change QA should fail this PR for, per the decision recorded in approach.
Do not fail this PR for the PR-title [AI] prefix: the title is generated by .sdlc/bin/open-pr.mjs:138 and is not this diff's to set.
risks: The reworded sentence is prose, so no test can prove it correct — AC-1 and AC-2 are read-and-grep checks a human or reviewer has to actually perform. The risk is not that the comment breaks; it is that a plausible rewrap lands that is wrong in some new way, which is why exact replacement text is given rather than described.

If the implementer substitutes the review's 'each test installs', the comment acquires a factual error it does not have today (only 5 of 10 tests install a console spy). QA step 3 is written to catch exactly this.

Keeping the release note leaves a user-facing changelog line describing a test-comment rewrap, which is what the reviewer objected to. Deliberate, not an oversight — see approach — and review may overturn it. If it does, delete the note whole; no rewrite of its body is wanted, because the body is accurate and the objection is to its existence.
This change touches nothing in forbidden_paths. Finding 3 would have (.sdlc/bin/open-pr.mjs), which is why it is out of scope rather than planned; the gate would refuse the whole plan for it.
No host is added to env.api_allowlist and no network behaviour changes. The diff is a comment inside a file that already runs in CI.
out_of_scope: Renaming PR #67 to add the [AI] prefix. Not a change this repository can make: the title is generated by .sdlc/bin/open-pr.mjs:138 (`'--title', `fix: ${issueData.title}``) with no [AI] in that file, which is why PRs #53, #59, #60, #64 and #65 share the shape. .sdlc/bin/** is forbidden_paths (.sdlc/config.yml:218) and .sdlc/** is framework. Recorded so it is not lost: whoever owns the pipeline should add [AI] at open-pr.mjs:138.

Adding a release note for this PR. The documented convention asks for one and the gate does not enforce it, but this change is a continuation of the comment rewrap the existing note already describes, and a second note saying the same thing is the accumulation the reviewer flagged. If the gate is ever wired into .github/workflows/, this diff would need a note (or an edit to the existing one, which counts under the check's AMR diff-filter) — that belongs with that work.

Any edit to index.electron.test.ts. Checked for the same attachment ambiguity; it has none — its comment at lines 42-45 makes no fetch-spy claim and describes the teardown's effect on the next test, not on the beforeAll.

Correcting the review's grep, which reported four console spies where there are five. The fifth (lines 116-118) is wrapped across three lines and a single-line search for 'vi.spyOn(console' misses it. The review's conclusion is unaffected — beforeAll still installs none — but AC-2 is written against the correct count.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: All three findings were checked against current main and all three still reproduce. Finding 1 is a single-clause rewording in one comment; the facts the reworded sentence asserts were each verified against the code (beforeAll at lines 17-21 installs only the fetch patch; the five console spies are all inside test bodies). Finding 3 is not reproducible as a code defect at all: its cause is pipeline plumbing in .sdlc/bin/open-pr.mjs, which this issue may not touch, so it is scoped out with evidence rather than planned. The 12 points of confidence not claimed are on the release-note call (finding 2), a judgement about a merged artefact and the one thing the review stage may reasonably overturn.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop the console clause from line 25 entirely, relying on the describe-level comment at lines 46-51 (the review's second option).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Lines 46-51 state how many tests spy console.log but not the beforeAll contrast, and the beforeAll contrast is the reason the comment at 23-31 exists — it explains why the beforeEach re-arms a patch the beforeAll already installed. Removing the clause loses the comment's point rather than clarifying it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Use the review's exact wording, '...along with the console spies each test installs'.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It states something false about the file: 5 of the 10 tests install a console spy (lines 81, 116-118, 160, 311, 379), so 'each test installs' is contradicted by the other five.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete upcoming-release-notes/clarify-sqljs-fetch-patch-test-comment.md, which is what the review's 'to drop it' option and PR #55's comment-only diff point toward.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The gate argument against keeping it is sound but not needed: packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:105 asks for a release note independently of any gate, and :120 explicitly exempts the Maintenance category from the non-technical rule. Deleting is a PR whose whole content is removing a published changelog entry — more visible than the entry — and it recurses, since that PR would itself want a note.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add the [AI] prefix to the PR title as part of this change, per the review's 'Fix' line.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The title is not hand-authored. .sdlc/bin/open-pr.mjs:138 builds it from the issue title as `fix: ${issueData.title}`, which is why five other PRs share the shape. Editing it here means editing .sdlc/bin/**, which is forbidden_paths (.sdlc/config.yml:218), and the gate would refuse the entire plan for one file in it.

assumptions: The review's findings were written against PR #67 as it stood and nothing since has touched them; verified individually against current main rather than assumed.
'Current main' is commit 6ee19f7 on branch main, which is what the checkout was at when this order was written.

upcoming-release-notes/ is the only place a note can live for the next release, and packages/docs/docs/upcoming-release-notes.md is generated from it at release time rather than committed — the file does not exist in this checkout, consistent with that.
unknowns: Whether the maintainer agrees that a Maintenance note may describe a test-comment rewrap. The documentation's exemption for the Maintenance category is explicit, but the review's reading — that this is the only note describing an edit to a comment — is a fair aesthetic objection about the public changelog, and a judgement about the product's voice rather than the code. That is why the route keeps a review stage and why this is recorded as a decision with its reasoning rather than a settled fact.

Whether the inert release-notes gate (.github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml exists, no workflow references it) is deliberate or an oversight. If an oversight, wiring it up would make the keep/drop decision load-bearing in a way it is not today, and would require every future comment-only PR to carry a note.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: No decisions were recorded for this issue and no prior plan was rejected, so there was nothing binding to work from — plan/brief.md is empty on both counts. The planning judgement was concentrated in finding 2, where the review explicitly declined to close a call and handed it forward: whether the release note stays now that the gate justifying it turns out to be inert. I closed it (keep) rather than deferring, because the implementer must not be left to make a product-voice judgement, and recorded the reasoning so review can reverse it cheaply. I diverged from the review's suggested replacement wording on finding 1, because that wording introduces a factual error the review itself did not check for.
residual_risks: A comment-only change carries a near-zero chance of breaking behaviour, and correspondingly a near-zero chance that the suite catches a mistake in it. AC-1 and AC-2 are the only real checks and both require someone to read the sentence against the code. If QA skips them because nothing failed, the change is unverified in the only sense that matters for it.

The release-note decision is the one part of this order a reasonable person could reverse after the fact. It is reversible at no cost — a single validated file that can be deleted whole in a later PR — but if reversed, the changelog changes and that later PR should say so.
